summary: This directory serves as the root architectural layer, coordinating business logic, domain state management, and a unified UI rendering infrastructure. It ensures consistent component behavior and data integrity by decoupling domain models from specific third-party UI library implementations.
responsibilities: Manage core business workflows and state transitions
Define abstract rendering contracts for UI components
Consolidate and export the application's design system
Enforce business invariants and validation rules
Decouple domain logic from infrastructure and UI implementation
relationships: Domain models provide the state that business logic and workflows operate upon.
The renderer contract decouples generic UI requirements from concrete third-party component libraries.
Centralized exports allow the application to consume UI elements and layout abstractions through a unified entry point.
Business rules define the constraints and logic applied during state transitions managed by the hooks layer.
UI adapters translate application requirements into consistent representations by consuming the defined renderer contracts.
designDecisions: Adoption of the adapter pattern to isolate application logic from UI library dependencies.
Use of barrel export patterns to simplify component discovery and consumption.
Separation of concerns between data state and business orchestration.
Interface-driven development to ensure structural consistency across rendering implementations.
Domain-driven design to segregate core business logic from visual presentation.
